tex_content.html:
\begin{exercise} \end{exercise}1. ch10:10-23Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold, and suppose $p,q \in M$ are points such that $d_g(p,q)$ is equal to the distance from $p$ to its cut locus.

  1. Prove that either $q$ is conjugate to $p$ along some minimizing geodesic segment, or there are exactly two minimizing geodesic segments from $p$ to $q$, say $\gamma _1, \gamma _2: [0,b] \to M$, such that $\gamma '_1(b) = -\gamma '_2(b)$.

  2. Now suppose in addition that $\text{inj}(p) = \text{inj}(M)$. Prove that if $q$ is not conjugate to $p$ along any minimizing geodesic, then there is a closed geodesic $\gamma : [0,2b] \to M$ such that $\gamma (0) = \gamma (2b) = p$ and $\gamma (b) = q$, where $b = d_g(p,q)$.

(Used on p. 343.) \end{exercise}
